title: Split the every-manifest-command sweep per command group (its 15s bound is already marginal on dev)
description:
test/cli-tracker-process.test.ts invokes EVERY manifest command inside two tests, each under a 15s per-test bound (invokeEveryManifestPayloadCommand in cli-tracker-process.test.ts, the sweeps "renders more than its kind" and "principal null as its last JSON key"). The bound is a hang detector, and clean dev ALONE already reached 14.73s under local contention (measured 2026-10-14). The sweep grows with every command added to the manifest: the QCLI-445 branch added five question commands and reached 15.06s once.

Ruling (team-lead, 2026-10-14): split the sweep per command group so each test bounds a group rather than the whole manifest, and NEVER raise the bound.

Evidence: isolated same-machine measurement, clean dev (b39314ce) min 6.28 / median 9.2-10.5 / max 14.73; QCLI-445 branch min 7.82 / median 9.08-10.90 / max 15.06 (n>=10). Full table in the opum-ai/quest-cli#615 body.
plan: 1. Read invokeEveryManifestPayloadCommand and the two sweep tests; identify the fixture set each command group needs.
2. Parameterize the sweep by a command-group slice; keep the fixture build and the manifest-order dependencies intact.
3. Define per-group tests bounding each group rather than the whole manifest; never raise the 15s bound.
4. Prove it fixes the object it claims: the per-group tests must go green and stay bounded on a contended machine.
5. Full check, then PR into dev.
implementationNotes: This PR also carries QCLI-503 (the format script now uses the explicit path list, so a .claude/worktrees review worktree no longer breaks bun run format) and the QCLI-502 filing. Both are named in the PR body.

Post-split sweep measurement, taken here because team-lead moved the bound question to QCLI-501: with #615 landed and this split rebased on top, each group test bounds one family and the 15s per-test bound is unchanged. Isolated, same machine: the heaviest group (task, 16 commands, harness built fresh per mode) is about 2.8s per test; question about 1.9s; registry about 2.3s -- against about 12s worst for the monolithic sweep on dev with #615 in. So the split buys roughly 5x headroom against the bound. QCLI-504 item (5) produced no bound change in its own PR, so there was nothing to drop from its diff; the bound is measured here, after the split, as directed.
